classification.description: Prettier is an opinionated code formatter.

plan.architecture_summary: Prettier is an opinionated code formatter implemented primarily in JavaScript. It parses source files into Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) using various language parsers and then re-prints them using a layout engine based on Wadler's pretty-printing paper. The source code is organized into core logic (`src/main`), configuration handling (`src/config`), CLI handling, and language-specific printers and formatters (`src/language-js`, `src/language-css`, etc.). Tests are primarily integration and snapshot tests located under `tests/format/`, run using Jest.

setup_steps.title: Run tests
setup_steps.detail: Run the test suite via Jest to verify the setup.

pull_request: Add a unreleased changelog entry under changelog_unreleased/ following the template.
code_style: Run `yarn fix` to automatically lint with ESLint and format with Prettier.
Run `yarn lint` to check types, linting, spelling, changelogs, etc.

issues.title: Non-idempotent: `delete` of a JSDoc-cast member needs two passes
issues.why: A clear JavaScript formatting issue involving non-idempotency with JSDoc casts, perfect for a JavaScript beginner looking at AST formatting.
issues.approach: Investigate why formatting a `delete` expression with a JSDoc type cast drops parentheses on the first pass and adds them back differently on the second pass, then fix the comment/parenthesization or printing logic in JavaScript formatting.

issues.title: Unstable comment print in parenthesized arrow function body
issues.why: A targeted issue with JavaScript arrow functions and comment idempotency.
issues.approach: Examine why comment printing inside parenthesized arrow function bodies leads to unstable prints across passes, and adjust comment attachment or printing rules.

issues.title: SCSS: inline comment before nested function adds extra indent
issues.why: A scoped styling issue in SCSS comment printing suitable for someone familiar with JavaScript/TypeScript logic.
issues.approach: Investigate why an inline comment before a nested function in SCSS adds an extra indent, and adjust the comment handling or printer indentation logic for SCSS/CSS.

first_timer_insights: First-time contributors successfully landed PRs ranging from simple typo fixes and documentation updates to test additions and small bug fixes in comment printing or configuration caching.
Successful PRs include a changelog file in changelog_unreleased/ and relevant test cases.
caveats: Some complex comment-handling and AST idempotency issues may require deep familiarity with internal printing invariants and parser AST structures.
